# Job Chapter 4 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 417r–417v

---

**4:1** And-answered Elifaz [Eliphaz] the-Teimanite and-said:

**4:2** "If-one-ventures [ha-nissah] a-word [davar] to-you, will-you-be-weary [til'eh]?
But to-restrain [latsor] words [millim] who is-able [yukhal]?

**4:3** Behold, you-have-instructed [yissarta] many [rabbim],
and-hands [yadayim] weak [rafot] you-have-strengthened [techazzeq].

**4:4** The-stumbling-one [koshel] your-words [milleykha] would-raise-up [yeqimun],
and-knees [birkayim] bowing [kor'ot] you-would-strengthen [te'ammets].

**4:5** But now it-comes to-you and-you-are-weary [til'eh];
it-touches [tiga] you and-you-are-dismayed [tibbahel].

**4:6** Is-not your-fear [yir'atkha] your-confidence [kislatekha],
your-hope [tiqvatekha] — and-the-integrity [tom] of-your-ways?

**4:7** Remember [zekhor] now — who [is] the-innocent [naqi] who-perished [avad]?
And-where [were] the-upright [yesharim] cut-off [nikhchadu]?

**4:8** As I-have-seen [ra'itiy], the-ones-plowing [chorshei] iniquity [aven]
and-the-ones-sowing [zore'ei] trouble [amal] — they-reap-it [yiqtseruhu].

**4:9** By-the-breath [mi-nishmat] of-God [eloah] they-perish [yovedu],
and-by-the-spirit [me-ruach] of-his-anger [appo] they-are-consumed [yikhlu].

**4:10** The-roar [sha'agat] of-the-lion [aryeh] and-the-voice of-the-fierce-lion [shachal],
and-the-teeth [shinnei] of-the-young-lions [kefirim] are-broken [nitte'u].

**4:11** The-lion [layish] perishes [oved] for-lack of-prey [teref],
and-the-cubs [benei] of-the-lioness [lavi] are-scattered [yitparredu].

**4:12** And-to-me a-word [davar] was-brought-secretly [yegunav],
and-received [vattiqach] my-ear [ozniy] a-whisper [shemets] of-it.

**4:13** In-thoughts [bi-se'ippim] from-visions [me-chezyonot] of-the-night [laylah],
when-falls [bi-nfol] deep-sleep [tardemah] upon men [anashim],

**4:14** dread [pachad] met-me [qera'aniy] and-trembling [ure'adah],
and-the-multitude of-my-bones [atsmotay] it-caused-to-tremble [hifchid].

**4:15** And-a-spirit [ve-ruach] passed-over [yachalof] my-face [panay];
it-caused-to-stand-up [tesammeir] the-hair of-my-flesh [sa'arat besariy].

**4:16** It-stood [ya'amod] and-I-could-not recognize [lo akir] its-appearance [mar'ehu];
a-form [temunah] before my-eyes [le-neged einay];
silence [demamah] — and-a-voice [qol] I-heard [eshma]:

**4:17** 'Can-a-mortal [enosh] be-righteous [yitsddaq] before-God [me-eloah]?
Can-a-man [gever] be-pure [yithar] before his-Maker [me-osehu]?

**4:18** Behold, in-his-servants [ba-avadav] he-does-not trust [lo ya'amin],
and-to-his-angels [malakhav] he-charges [yasim] error [tohlah].

**4:19** How-much-more [af] the-dwellers [shoknei] of-houses of-clay [batei chomer],
whose foundation [yessodam] [is] in-the-dust [ba-afar];
they-are-crushed [yedakke'um] before [lifnei] a-moth [ash].

**4:20** From-morning [mi-boqer] to-evening [la-erev] they-are-shattered [yukattu];
without anyone-noticing [mi-beli mesim], forever [la-netsach] they-perish [yovedu].

**4:21** Is-not pulled-away [nissa] their-tent-cord [yitram] within-them?
They-die [yamutu] and-not in-wisdom [ve-lo be-chokhmah].'

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.6 — "Is not your fear your confidence?":** The Hebrew *yir'ah* can mean both "fear" (dread) and "fear of God" (piety). Elifaz is appealing to Iyyov's well-known piety as the foundation for hope — but the ambiguity is telling.

**v.12-16 — The night vision:** This passage is among the most haunting in the Hebrew Bible. The vocabulary of secrecy (*yegunav*, stolen), whisper (*shemets*), deep sleep (*tardemah*, the same word used of Adam's sleep in Genesis 2:21), and the hair standing on end creates an atmosphere of numinous dread.

**v.17 — "*enosh* before God":** The word *enosh* (mortal, frail human) rather than *adam* (human) emphasizes humanity's weakness. The question — "Can a mortal be righteous before God?" — is the theological backbone of Elifaz's argument.

---
*— EMET*
